papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Standard [¹⁸F]FDG PET/CT has suboptimal sensitivity for assessing viable brain metastases due to high physiological brain background. Fibroblast activation protein (FAP)-targeted PET, with minimal brain expression, may overcome this limitation. This study aimed to compare the diagnostic performance of [⁶⁸Ga]Ga-FAPI-2286 versus [¹⁸F]FDG PET/CT for detecting viable brain metastases in lung cancer and evaluate their complementary value. METHODS: In this prospective intra-individual study, 24 lung cancer patients with brain metastases underwent both [⁶⁸Ga]Ga-FAPI-2286 and [¹⁸F]FDG PET/CT within 3 days. Images were independently and blindly reviewed by two senior nuclear medicine physicians. Diagnostic performance (sensitivity, specificity, accuracy) was evaluated per-lesion and per-patient against a composite reference standard (characteristic imaging features, ≥ 3-month follow-up, comprehensive clinical evaluation). Quantitative parameters (SUVmax, target-to-background ratio [TBR], background uptake [SUVbgd]) and complementary detection patterns were analyzed. RESULTS: Among 43 lesions (36 viable, 7 non-viable), [⁶⁸Ga]Ga-FAPI-2286 demonstrated significantly higher per-lesion sensitivity (83.3% vs. 75.0%, P = 0.032) and accuracy (86.0% vs. 79.1%, P = 0.002) than [¹⁸F]FDG. Per-patient sensitivity (89.5% vs. 73.7%, P = 0.004) and accuracy (91.7% vs. 79.2%, P = 0.003) were also superior. The AUC for [⁶⁸Ga]Ga-FAPI-2286 was 0.917 (95% CI: 0.834-0.999) versus 0.875 (95% CI: 0.772-0.978) for [¹⁸F]FDG (P = 0.031). [⁶⁸Ga]Ga-FAPI-2286 provided dramatically higher TBR in viable lesions (85.39 ± 57.99 vs. 5.19 ± 2.56, P < 0.001) due to minimal physiological brain background (SUVbgd 0.09 ± 0.11). Dual-tracer imaging supplemented the detection of 15 viable tumor lesions in 9 patients that were missed by either single tracer alone, increasing per-lesion sensitivity to 100% and preventing potential underdiagnosis in 47.4% (9/19) of patients with viable disease. CONCLUSIONS: [⁶⁸Ga]Ga-FAPI-2286 PET/CT outperforms [¹⁸F]FDG in identifying viable brain metastases from lung cancer, primarily due to its exceptional tumor-to-background contrast. The complementary detection patterns of the two tracers suggest that combined use can minimize diagnostic omissions, supporting an integrative imaging paradigm for more accurate intracranial staging/restaging. TRIAL REGISTRATION: Registered 10 October 2022, https://www.chictr.org.cn , ChiCTR2100044131.

papers.abstract_en: Thymoma-associated myasthenia gravis (TAMG) complicates perioperative management because neurological vulnerability must be weighed against the physiological demands of tumor resection. This review examines operation-specific assessment and rapid immune optimization, compares established treatments with emerging neonatal Fc receptor (FcRn) inhibition, and proposes a dual-axis framework integrating myasthenia gravis (MG)-related vulnerability and anticipated operative burden. Intravenous immunoglobulin and plasma exchange remain the established rapid-treatment options when clinically meaningful improvement is needed before surgery. FcRn inhibition provides a mechanistically distinct means of lowering circulating immunoglobulin G. Among FcRn inhibitors, efgartigimod has the most direct perioperative evidence in TAMG, but available studies are small, nonrandomized, and largely confined to selected adults with acetylcholine receptor antibody-positive disease undergoing planned surgery. No randomized trial or TAMG-specific active-comparator study has demonstrated that perioperative efgartigimod reduces postoperative myasthenic crisis or other surgical complications. Its optimal preoperative schedule and the value of routine postoperative continuation remain uncertain. Decisions about rapid immune optimization should consider the recent MG trajectory, bulbar and respiratory function, secretion clearance, operative demands, and available postoperative support. Surgical readiness requires multidisciplinary judgment tailored to the planned operation; it cannot be determined by a single clinical score, antibody level, or predetermined treatment course. The proposed dual-axis framework is intended to structure this discussion but has not been validated.

papers.authors: Guo K, Sun Y, Deng J, Tang J, Zhao J, Zhang X, Yan Y, Yuan L et al.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Severe pneumonia is common among patients admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU). Herpes simplex virus (HSV) reactivation is frequently detected in patients with severe pneumonia, particularly in immunocompromised individuals. Although metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) enables rapid and broad-spectrum pathogen detection, the clinical significance of bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) mNGS-defined HSV reactivation in immunocompromised patients with severe pneumonia remains unclear. METHODS: This retrospective multicenter cohort study included 350 adults admitted to ICUs at five hospitals with severe pneumonia between November 2021 and November 2025. BALF for mNGS was obtained within 24 hours after ICU admission. HSV-1 reactivation was operationally classified as BALF mNGS HSV-1 DNA positivity using a prespecified viral RPM-r threshold ≥3.0; this definition does not establish HSV pneumonia. The primary endpoint was 28-day mortality measured from ICU admission. A multivariable logistic regression model evaluated the association of HSV with mortality and modification of this association by immune status. RESULTS: Among 350 patients, 144 (41.14%) were immunocompromised and 206 (58.86%) were immunocompetent. HSV-1 reactivation was identified in 51/144 (35.42%) and 35/206 (16.99%) patients, respectively (P < 0.001). Among immunocompromised patients, 28-day mortality was 32/51 (62.75%) with HSV reactivation and 34/93 (36.56%) without it (Fisher exact P = 0.003). The corresponding rates in immunocompetent patients were 8/35 (22.86%) and 56/171 (32.75%); no statistically significant association was observed (Fisher exact P = 0.318). The adjusted HSV-by-immune-status interaction was statistically significant (OR = 4.451, 95% CI 1.449-13.668; P = 0.009). From the overall adjusted interaction model, the HSV-associated OR was 2.622 (95% CI 1.275-5.395) in immunocompromised patients and 0.589 (95% CI 0.249-1.394) in immunocompetent patients. In a separate model restricted to immunocompromised patients, the adjusted HSV-associated OR was 2.403 (95% CI 1.155-5.002; P = 0.019). The observed association with CMV co-detection within the HSV-positive subgroup was exploratory. CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with severe pneumonia, BALF mNGS-defined HSV-1 reactivation was associated with higher 28-day mortality in immunocompromised patients, while no statistically significant association was observed in immunocompetent patients. Immune status modified the observed association on the odds-ratio scale. These findings are observational and do not establish HSV pneumonia, a causal effect of HSV, benefit from earlier mNGS testing, or an indication for antiviral therapy.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Pulmonary hypertension (PH) mortality may not have followed recent improvements in tobacco-related diseases. We compared PH mortality with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and lung cancer and assessed whether divergence was specific to deaths with documented tobacco use. RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS: We analyzed Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) WONDER mortality data for US residents aged ≥ 25 years. PH required I27.0 or I27.2 as the underlying cause; COPD and lung cancer formed the benchmark. Age-adjusted mortality-rate ratios for 2018-2024 were modeled using inverse-variance weighting, restricted maximum likelihood, and Knapp-Hartung inference. A post hoc analysis removed the tobacco-documentation requirement. RESULTS: Among tobacco-documented deaths, PH mortality showed no clear linear change (annual percent change, 0.50%; 95% confidence interval (CI), -1.55% to 2.59%), whereas benchmark mortality declined (-4.83%; 95% CI, -5.51% to -4.15%). The PH-to-benchmark rate ratio increased 5.59% annually (ratio of annual rate ratios, 1.056; 95% CI, 1.035-1.078; p = 0.001). The unrestricted estimate was nearly identical (1.056; 95% CI, 1.032-1.080). CONCLUSIONS: Recent PH mortality diverged from improving COPD and lung-cancer mortality. Because the unrestricted comparison yielded a nearly identical estimate, the divergence cannot be considered tobacco-specific. Death certificates cannot establish smoking exposure, PH phenotype, or causality.

papers.authors: Iliakis CS, T'Jonck W, Mouat IC, McCowan J, Burden Z, Hegarty LM, Bankole S, Liang J et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Immunoregulation Laboratory, The Francis Crick Institute, London, UK.

papers.abstract_en: Alveolar macrophages (AMs) form a first line of defense to lung insults. These insults often lead to replacement of fetal-derived tissue-resident AMs (fAMs) by monocyte-derived AMs (mono-AMs) with different functionality, which impacts lung immunity during future lung challenges. However, whether these alterations are conserved or insult specific is not well understood. Here we show that respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection remodels the AM compartment long term. We perform comparative analyses of fAMs and mono-AMs after RSV infection, influenza A virus infection or clodronate liposome administration and identify a crucial tissue integration checkpoint of CD11b+ mono-AMs that involves acquisition of proliferative capacity and requires EGR2-mediated transcriptional rewiring. Mono-AMs elicited by RSV, influenza A virus or clodronate liposomes have a hardwired ontogeny-dependent stereotypical profile of transcription, proliferation, metabolism and enhanced immunoreactivity despite a substantially different inflammatory environment during differentiation; accordingly, mono-AMs elicited by sterile or infectious insult protect from subsequent Streptococcus pneumoniae infection. By contrast, fAMs display context-dependent transcriptional alterations. Our findings highlight that long-term changes in the AM compartment show origin-dependent phenotypic divergence and that mono-AM integration follows a hardwired trajectory fine-tuned by environmental factors.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Pleural mesothelioma (PM) is a rare and aggressive malignancy in which therapeutic progress depends on a limited clinical trial evidence base. Although trial registration has improved transparency, the extent to which registered trials generate publicly available and clinically interpretable evidence remains unclear. We evaluated results reporting, primary endpoint achievement, and trial characteristics according to reporting status in registered interventional therapeutic trials for PM. METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional analysis of registered interventional therapeutic trials for PM on ClinicalTrials.gov from 2005 to 2025. Trial characteristics, completion status, public results reporting, and whether the prespecified primary endpoint was met were abstracted from ClinicalTrials.gov and complementary public sources. Reporting and primary-endpoint analyses included trials with a primary completion date at least 12 months before data abstraction. Trials were considered reported if results were publicly available from any source. Primary endpoint achievement was defined according to whether the prespecified primary endpoint was reported as met, without reclassification based on perceived clinical relevance or secondary outcomes. Trial characteristics were compared descriptively according to reporting status using Fisher exact tests. RESULTS: We identified 150 interventional therapeutic trials, representing a planned cumulative enrollment of 12,406 participants. Immunotherapy-containing strategies increased from 2.7% of trials in 2005-2015 to 39.5% in 2016-2025. Among 114 trials that had reached primary completion, 28 (24.6%) had no publicly available results. In descriptive comparisons, nonreporting was more frequent among trials with planned enrollment below 50 participants and among nonrandomized studies. Among 86 trials with reported results, the prespecified primary endpoint was met in 33 (38.4%), not met in 41 (47.7%), and not evaluable in 12 (14.0%). Among randomized trials with classifiable primary-endpoint status, 9 of 27 (33.3%) met their prespecified primary endpoint. CONCLUSIONS: Registered interventional therapeutic trials for PM have increasingly shifted toward immunotherapy-containing strategies; however, incomplete public reporting and the limited proportion of reported randomized trials with classifiable outcomes that met their prespecified primary endpoints constrain clinical interpretation.

papers.abstract_en: High-dose EGFR-TKIs have been used as an exploratory therapeutic strategy to overcome the limitations of the standard-dose regimen in the treatment of EGFR-mutant NSCLC, particularly in patients with CNS metastases. Available clinical evidence suggests that high-dose TKIs confer certain therapeutic efficacy and manageable safety profiles, with a small proportion of patients experiencing ≥3 grade adverse events, such as rash, nausea,diarrhea, aminotransferase rise, leukopenia.However, the evidence is limited by the predominance of single-center retrospective studies, small sample sizes, heterogeneous patient populations and short follow-up periods. Further large-scale, multicenter studies with long-term follow-up are needed to define more clearly the efficacy, safety, and appropriate clinical role of high-dose EGFR-TKI therapy.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality and imposes a substantial clinical and medical burden. Short-term exposure to ambient air pollutants can trigger exacerbations and increase healthcare use and costs. However, the avoidable COPD burden attributable to short-term air pollution exposure remains poorly quantified, especially in northwestern China. Comprehensive quantification of this burden is essential to inform targeted air quality and public health policies. METHODS: This time-stratified case-crossover study analyzed 37,868 COPD-related hospital admissions and 26,473 outpatient visits in Gansu Province during 2019, using data from Gansu Healthcare Security Administration and the ChinaHighAirPollutants dataset. Conditional logistic regression models were used to assess the link between ambient air pollutants and COPD admissions/visits, with measurements of excess fractions, medical fees, and length of stay calculated. RESULTS: Short-term exposure to PM2.5, NO2, CO, and O3 was associated with increased risks of COPD hospitalization and outpatient visits. In counterfactual modeling analyses assuming pollutant concentrations were reduced to WHO guideline levels, the modeled avoidable COPD burden was 9.19% [95% empirical confidence interval (eCI): 6.45%-11.94%] of hospital admissions, 3,481 (2,442-4,521) admissions, 25,899 (18,168-33,629) in-hospital days, 12.07 (8.46-15.67) million Chinese Yuan (CNY) in hospitalization costs, 8.40% (5.77%-11.03%) of outpatient visits, 2,224 (1,529-2,919) outpatient visits, and 0.25 (0.17-0.33) million CNY in outpatient costs. With WHO air quality guideline levels as the counterfactual reference, PM2.5 accounted for the largest proportion of the modeled avoidable inpatient COPD burden, whereas O3 accounted for the largest proportion of the modeled avoidable outpatient COPD burden. Under the theoretical minimum exposure scenario, O3 was the dominant contributor to outpatient burden, while PM2.5 and O3 contributed comparably to inpatient burden. CONCLUSIONS: Under WHO guideline scenario, PM2.5 and O3 mainly contributed to avoidable inpatient and outpatient COPD burden, respectively; under theoretical minimum exposure scenario, PM2.5 and O3 contributed comparably to inpatient burden, whereas O3 was the dominant contributor to outpatient burden.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Lymphangioleiomyomatosis (LAM) is a rare, progressive systemic disease characterized by diffuse cystic destruction of the lung parenchyma. Reliable markers of disease severity and progression remain limited. Quantitative assessment of cyst burden on chest computed tomography (CT) may provide objective information on disease status. AIM OF THE STUDY: To evaluate a fully automated method for cyst quantification and to investigate its clinical associations with disease severity and subsequent pulmonary function decline in patients with LAM. METHODS: In this retrospective study including patients from two European centers, clinical data from 74 patients with LAM were analyzed (Heidelberg, n = 54; Budapest, n = 20). Automated CT analysis was feasible in 63 patients. The cyst volume index (CVI), defined as the percentage of total lung volume occupied by cysts, was quantified using the fully automated software Yet Another CT Analyzer (YACTA). Associations between CVI and clinical, laboratory, and pulmonary function parameters were assessed. Multivariable linear regression was used to investigate the association between baseline CVI and annual change in FEV₁ Results: CVI correlated inversely with FEV₁ (rₛ = -0.58), FEV₁/FVC (rₛ = -0.72), and diffusing capacity for carbon monoxide (DLCOSB; rₛ = -0.59; all p < 0.001). In multivariable analysis, higher baseline CVI was independently associated with a greater annual FEV₁ decline (p = 0.028). A CVI ≥1.5% was associated with higher, but non-significant, odds of progression, defined as an annual FEV₁ decline of ≥90 mL (OR = 4.35, 95% CI 0.86-22.06; p = 0.076). CONCLUSION: Automated CT quantification of cystic lung destruction provides objective information on disease severity in LAM. Higher CVI was independently associated with subsequent FEV₁ decline, whereas its ability to classify progression was limited. Prospective studies are needed to validate the prognostic relevance of CVI.

papers.abstract_en: Tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) have transformed the treatment of EGFR-mutant non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), yet acquired resistance remains a major clinical limitation. Resistance is increasingly understood as an evolving state shaped not only by tumor-cell genomic alterations but also by treatment-induced remodeling of the tumor immune microenvironment (TIME). This Review examines how EGFR-TKI exposure reshapes macrophage states, T-cell function and localization, fibroblast and myeloid niches, and vascular architecture, and how these changes are reinforced by immune-checkpoint adaptation, metabolic reprogramming, and phenotypic plasticity. We then connect the evolving TIME to post-TKI therapeutic strategies according to the maturity of the supporting evidence, including immune checkpoint inhibitor-containing regimens, anti-angiogenic combinations, mechanism-matched targeted therapy, antibody-drug conjugates, bispecific T-cell engagers, and selected preclinical microenvironment-directed approaches. Finally, we discuss circulating biomarkers, single-cell sequencing, and spatial profiling as tools for longitudinally defining resistant immune states. Viewing TKI resistance as a temporally evolving immune ecosystem provides a framework for linking resistance mechanism, immune phenotype, and treatment selection rather than treating progression as a purely genomic endpoint.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Severe community-acquired pneumonia (SCAP) progresses rapidly, is associated with poor prognosis. Early assessment and timely intervention are crucial for improving the short-term outcomes of patients this study aims to develop and validate a Nomogram prognostic prediction model for SCAP. METHODS: Clinical data of 1,316 patients with SCAP from the MIMIC-IV database were used as the training cohort, and 177 patients from the Affiliated Hospital of Soochow University served as the external validation cohort. Candidate variables were selected using LASSO regression, and independent predictors were identified by multivariable logistic regression to construct a nomogram. Model performance was evaluated through the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration curves, and decision curve analysis (DCA). RESULTS: The nomogram incorporated six variables, including albumin, total bilirubin, blood urea nitrogen, lactate, age, and the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR). It showed moderate ability, with an AUC of 0.718 (95% CI, 0.686-0.750) in the training cohort and 0.774 (95% CI, 0.703-0.844) in the validation cohort, both of which were higher than those of the APACHE II. Calibration curves demonstrated good agreement between predicted and observed outcomes, and DCA indicated the potential clinical utility of the nomogram. CONCLUSIONS: The NLR-based nomogram developed for predicting 28-day mortality in patients with SCAP showed moderate predictive performance and is simple to apply. After further validation, it may serve as a practical tool for early risk screening and triage.

papers.abstract_en: Fungal and bacterial dysbiosis are linked to asthma disease severity, yet how overgrowth of the commensal fungus Candida albicans contributes to disease progression is not fully understood. Here, we show that intestinal aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR) deficiency exacerbates house dust mite (HDM)-induced allergic airway disease (AAD) during oral Candida albicans colonization through enhanced IL-17 responsiveness and lung structural cell fucosylation. Intestinal AhR deficiency promotes exaggerated IL-17 responses that promotes neutrophil migration and accumulation in the lung and reshapes the gut microbiota, particularly reducing the abundance of Akkermansia muciniphila. Concurrently, increased fucosylation of lung structural cells enhances L-selectin glycan ligand biosynthesis, thereby promoting neutrophil adhesion and retention within inflamed lung tissue. These adherent neutrophils lead to mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative stress, and tissue injury in epithelial and endothelial compartments. Administration of A. muciniphila or its derived outer membrane vesicles (OMVs), as well as genetic deletion of Fut2, reduces lung fucosylation, suppresses neutrophil adhesion and NET formation, and attenuates Candida albicans-exacerbated AAD. Together, these findings show that intestinal AhR signaling remotely regulates an IL-17- gut microbiota-fucosylation axis that promotes neutrophil adhesion, mitochondrial dysfunction of lung structure cell, and neutrophilic airway inflammation during Candida albicans-associated asthma.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: chronic cough (CC) is a highly prevalent problem; its impact in patients treated in different settings is not known Research Question: Do CC characteristics and management differ between patients attending Pneumology and Geriatrics ambulatory care facilities for CC? METHODS: all patients attending 2 Pneumology and 2 Geriatrics clinics between October 2019 and July 2024 were consecutively enrolled and were compared with respect to comorbidities, drugs, CC seasonality and circadian rhythm, Leicester questionnaire (LCQ), VAS score of CC impact. RESULTS: 88 (mean age 73.3, SD 8.9, 67% females) and 312 (mean age 61.9, SD 15, 62.8% females) participants were enrolled in the Geriatrics and Pneumology groups, respectively. The impact of CC was greater in Pneumology, with mean LCQ total score = 14.9 (SD: 3.58) vs 17.8 (SD: 2.78). Compared to patients enrolled in Geriatrics, those enrolled in Pneumology more frequently reported worsening of cough in winter/spring and during the night. Most Geriatrics patients reported no CC-related symptoms, while dyspnea (25.3%), dizziness (5.1%), chest pain (10.2%) and vomitus (4.8%) were reported by Pneumology patients. Compared to the Pneumology population, specialist consultations were less common in the Geriatrics population; likewise, spirometry and CT scans were performed more frequently in the Pneumology than in the Geriatrics ambulatory. CC severity, as expressed by the VAS score, was directly correlated with number of comorbidities in patients attending Geriatrics clinics (Beta 0.37, 95% CI 0.105-0.634, P 0.007), but not in patients attending Pneumology clinics . CONCLUSIONS: CC is characterized by different profiles of severity, impact on health status and healthcare resource use, seasonality and intraday variation in patients attending Geriatrics and Pneumology clinics. Older people also showed a lower burden of diagnostic exams. Furthermore, in patients attending Geriatrics ambulatories CC severity is correlated with the number of chronic diseases as if CC did not have an autonomous impact as in their counterpart attending Pneumology ambulatories.

papers.abstract_en: Undernutrition is the leading risk factor for tuberculosis susceptibility, severity, and poor treatment outcome. Nutritional immunology and immunometabolism frame how nutrient availability and metabolism shape host defense against Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) infection. By integrating targeted metabolomics and transcriptional profiling in a murine tuberculosis model, we defined immunometabolic programs underlying the transition from acute to chronic infection. Immune control of Mtb during acute infection was accompanied by robust activation of immune and metabolic programs, including mTORC1-associated signaling, glutaminolysis, glycolysis, arginine metabolism, and serine one-carbon metabolism, thereby highlighting the importance of amino acid metabolism and mitochondrial function in antimicrobial immunity. In contrast, chronic infection was characterized by reduced immune activation and mTORC1-associated signaling, increased branched-chain amino acid catabolism, and altered amino acid profiles, with leucine and glutamine among the discriminating metabolites. These findings suggest that reduced glutamine availability during chronic infection may increase reliance on leucine oxidative catabolism to sustain mitochondrial metabolism during nutrient stress, potentially limiting leucine availability for mTORC1-associated anabolic metabolism and immune activation. Oral glutamine supplementation restored amino acid homeostasis, including lung leucine abundance, enhanced mTORC1-associated signaling and central metabolic programs, moderately reduced bacterial burden and lung pathology, and mitigated infection-associated wasting. Reanalysis of published human metabolomics datasets further demonstrated reduced circulating glutamine levels during progression to active tuberculosis, supporting conservation of glutamine metabolic dysregulation across host species. Collectively, our findings identify a potential glutamine-leucine metabolic axis linking nutrient availability with immunometabolic competence and provide a mechanistic rationale for evaluating glutamine supplementation as a host-directed strategy for tuberculosis.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Pulmonary alveolar proteinosis (PAP) is a rare and heterogeneous lung disease characterized by the accumulation of surfactant-derived lipoproteinaceous material within the alveoli. The clinical features, diagnostic approaches, and management strategies of PAP remain variable, and a comprehensive synthesis of published clinical evidence is lacking. OBJECTIVE: To systematically summarize the current clinical characteristics, diagnostic patterns, and treatment strategies of PAP based on published case reports and clinical studies. METHODS: A scoping review was conducted by searching multiple databases from inception to 2025. Studies reporting clinical data on PAP were included. Data were extracted and descriptively analyzed in terms of patient characteristics, diagnostic methods, clinical manifestations, auxiliary examinations, treatment approaches, and outcomes. RESULTS: A total of 785 studies involving 7,729 patients were included. Most studies were descriptive (737 studies, 93.9%), and 4,929 male and 2,800 female patients were reported, corresponding to a male-to-female ratio of approximately 1.76:1. Smoking (n = 3,095) and dust or occupational exposure (n = 633) were frequently reported. The most commonly reported symptoms were cough (n = 2,719), exertional dyspnea (n = 1,396), and sputum production (n = 1,375). Disease subtype information was available for 1,403 patients, of whom 1,311 (93.4%) had primary PAP; among patients with primary PAP, 1,242 (94.7%) had autoimmune PAP. Laboratory, imaging, pulmonary function, and bronchoscopy data were available for 71.7%, 67.8%, 54.0%, and 21.2% of patients, respectively. Among 2,909 patients with treatment information, WLL was the most frequently reported treatment (1,928 patients, 66.3%), followed by corticosteroid therapy (325, 11.2%) and GM-CSF therapy (232, 8.0%). CONCLUSIONS: Current evidence on PAP is dominated by descriptive studies and marked by substantial gaps in diagnostic standardization and disease classification. Clinical manifestations are largely nonspecific, and laboratory and functional assessments are inconsistently reported. Whole lung lavage remains the mainstay of management, but high-quality evidence to guide diagnosis and treatment remains limited.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: Short-term unplanned readmission is common after hospitalization for acute exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (AECOPD). We assessed whether admission aggregate index of systemic inflammation (AISI), derived from routine blood counts, is associated with unplanned AECOPD-related readmission. PATIENTS AND METHODS: This retrospective cohort included 1,702 patients discharged after AECOPD hospitalization between January 1, 2023, and December 1, 2025. The primary outcome was 90-day unplanned AECOPD-related readmission; 30- and 60-day readmissions were secondary. We used Cox regression, restricted cubic splines, subgroup and sensitivity analyses, and Fine-Gray regression with death as a competing event, and assessed incremental predictive performance against a clinical model. RESULTS: Within 90 days, 190 patients (11.2%) were readmitted. In the primary analysis, the hazard ratio (HR) per one-unit increase in ln(AISI) was 1.17 (95% confidence interval [CI], 1.01-1.35); HRs at 30 and 60 days were 1.33 (1.07-1.64) and 1.22 (1.03-1.45), respectively. The exploratory median-based 90-day HR was 1.54 (1.15-2.07). The competing-risk subdistribution HR was 1.17 (1.00-1.37; P=0.054). The overall spline association was significant, without significant nonlinearity (P=0.019 and P=0.071). Point estimates were directionally consistent across sensitivity analyses, but the association became nonsignificant after excluding hospital stays ≤3 or ≥30 days (HR, 1.10; 95% CI, 0.94-1.28) and after adjustment for glucocorticoid and antibiotic use (HR, 1.09; 0.94-1.27). Adding ln(AISI) increased the apparent 90-day area under the curve from 0.632 to 0.640; the continuous net reclassification improvement and integrated discrimination improvement were not significant (P=0.079 and P=0.180). CONCLUSION: Higher admission AISI was associated with unplanned AECOPD-related readmission within 30, 60, and 90 days after discharge, and the association was directionally consistent in competing-risk and most sensitivity analyses, although it was not significant after length-of-stay restriction or glucocorticoid and antibiotic adjustment. AISI added little discrimination beyond conventional variables, and its clinical utility remains uncertain; prospective multicenter validation is needed before routine use.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: In patients with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF), supplemental oxygen may improve symptoms but may also place a burden on patients. We investigated changes in quality of life and exercise capacity following initiation of supplemental oxygen, and associations between initiating oxygen and clinical outcomes, in patients with IPF. METHODS: We used data from the IPF-PRO Registry to evaluate changes in St. George's Respiratory Questionnaire (SGRQ) total and domain scores, Cough and Sputum Assessment Questionnaire (CASA-Q) cough impact and symptoms domain scores and 6-minute walk test distance (6MWD) in patients with IPF before and after initiation of oxygen using linear regression (adjusted for lung function before oxygen initiation). We evaluated associations between initiation of oxygen and risk of clinical outcomes using Cox models. RESULTS: Among 611 patients, 343 (56.1%) initiated oxygen with activity and 245 (40.1%) initiated oxygen with activity and at rest (median follow-up: 51.5 months). There were significant mean increases (worsenings) in SGRQ total, activity and impact scores of 5.7, 7.3, and 5.1, respectively, after initiation of oxygen with activity, and in SGRQ total, activity, impact and symptoms scores of 8.6, 9.5, 8.2, and 6.9, respectively, after initiation of oxygen with activity and at rest. There was a significant mean decrease (worsening) in CASA-Q cough impact score of 6.4 after initiation of oxygen with activity and at rest. There were non-significant decreases in 6MWD (m) of 41.0 and 52.4, respectively, after initiation of oxygen with activity and initiation of oxygen with activity and at rest. Risks of subsequent respiratory hospitalization, death or lung transplant, and death were significantly greater among patients who did versus did not initiate oxygen. CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with IPF, worsening of quality of life and exercise capacity were observed following initiation of supplemental oxygen. Clinical outcomes were worse in patients using than not using oxygen. These data provide further evidence that initiation of supplemental oxygen is a milestone in the patient journey in IPF, but should not be interpreted as showing that initiation of oxygen in itself has deleterious effects. papers.abstract_en: Mycobacterium tuberculosis (MTB) is distributed across diverse geographic environments, but whether high-altitude environments impose recurrent selective pressures on its genome remains unclear. Here, we assembled a geographically broad, phylogenetically matched MTB cohort spanning three major high-altitude systems and applied four complementary genomic analyses to characterize altitude-associated evolutionary signals. Across the 406 matched pairs, these analyses captured distinct but complementary signals across site, phylogenetic and gene levels, encompassing matched-pair association, homoplasy-based convergence, gene burden and gene-wise selection. We then summarized these evidence streams at the gene level and integrated them using a standardized weighted prioritization framework, yielding 321 Tier 1 high-confidence genes, including 229 supported by all four evidence layers. Functional enrichment analysis of high-altitude-favoured Tier 1 genes revealed significant concentration in cell envelope/lipid metabolism and cofactor/intermediary metabolism, with pathway-level signals involving mycolic acid biosynthesis, glyoxylate and dicarboxylate metabolism, and porphyrin metabolism. Co-hit analysis further identified coordinated relationships linking envelope remodeling, transport, redox adaptation and genome maintenance. In two independent hypoxic-culture Tn-seq screens, 29 of 321 Tier 1 genes showed significant fitness effects in at least one screen, and 10 supported in both including Rv3680, fadD31, ppm1, pssA, ansA, mbtB, mbtD, adhC, drrA, and Rv2030c. These findings support convergent adaptation of MTB to high-altitude environments, with evolutionary signals centred on a high-confidence candidate core organized around cell-envelope remodeling, metabolic reprogramming and persistence-related stress survival.

papers.abstract_en: Aspergillus fumigatus is a major opportunistic fungal pathogen whose ability to maintain hyphal integrity and withstand host defenses is critical for virulence. Septal pores, which connect hyphal compartments, are dynamically regulated to preserve cellular integrity under stress, yet the molecular components governing this process remain incompletely defined. Here, we identify and characterize a septal pore-associated protein, SppA, and demonstrate its essential role in maintaining septal integrity in A. fumigatus. We show that expression of SppA is positively regulated by the transcription factor ZfpA and is induced in response to the cell wall-targeting antifungal caspofungin. Deletion of sppA resulted in defective septal organization and increased susceptibility to hyphal damage. The mutant exhibited heightened sensitivity to cell wall-targeting antifungal agents, indicating a role in cell wall stress tolerance. In a zebrafish model of invasive aspergillosis, loss of SppA significantly attenuated virulence which was abrogated in neutrophil-deficient zebrafish. Further, the mutant strain displayed increased susceptibility to killing by primary human neutrophils, suggesting that proper septal pore formation contributes to fungal survival during host immune attack. Together, our findings establish SppA as a critical determinant of septal integrity, antifungal tolerance, and pathogenicity in A. fumigatus, and position it as part of a ZfpA-regulated, caspofungin-responsive pathway that supports fungal survival during stress and infection.

papers.abstract_en: Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) remains a major cause of cancer-related mortality, and activating epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) mutations define a clinically important molecular subtype. EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) have substantially improved outcomes, but acquired resistance eventually limits long-term disease control. Among diverse resistance mechanisms, fibroblast growth factor receptor (FGFR) signaling has emerged as one of several potential bypass pathways. This review summarizes evidence implicating fibroblast growth factors (FGFs) and FGFRs in selected contexts of resistance to EGFR inhibition. Genetic alterations, including receptor fusions, amplifications, and activating mutations, and non-genetic mechanisms such as receptor overexpression and ligand-driven autocrine signaling may sustain downstream pathway activation. These processes can reactivate mitogenic and survival signaling despite EGFR inhibition and may support tumor persistence in a subset of molecular settings. We discuss preclinical and clinical evidence for FGFR-associated resistance, with particular emphasis on the functionally characterized FGF2-FGFR1 axis. Emerging therapeutic strategies, including selective FGFR inhibitors, multi-kinase inhibitors, and investigational combination regimens with EGFR inhibitors or immunotherapy, are reviewed with attention to current limitations. Finally, we highlight challenges related to biomarker identification, routine testing, toxicity management, and clinical trial design, and outline future directions for evaluating FGFR-targeted approaches in EGFR-mutant NSCLC.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Granulocyte colony-stimulating factor (G-CSF) lung carcinoma is a rare and highly aggressive clinical entity characterized by persistent neutrophilia, high fever, and poor prognosis. Although the lung is a common primary site, the co-occurrence of G-CSF production and epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) mutations is extremely rare, particularly in squamous cell carcinoma (SCC). CASE PRESENTATION: A 79-year-old Asian man, a former smoker, presented with an 80 mm mass in the left upper lobe and was diagnosed with a G-CSF-producing lung SCC (cT4N2bM0, cStage IIIB). Genetic testing identified a minor mutation and high programmed death ligand 1 (PD-L1) expression (tumor proportion score: TPS 65%). Despite an initial partial response to concurrent chemoradiotherapy, the disease progressed rapidly during maintenance durvalumab therapy, with a marked secondary increase in serum G-CSF and interleukin 6 (IL-6) levels. Subsequent lines of therapy, including docetaxel and the EGFR-tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) afatinib and osimertinib, provided only transient or limited clinical benefits. The patient eventually succumbed to tumor progression 22 months after the initial diagnosis. DISCUSSION: To the best of our knowledge, this is the first English-language report of a G-CSF-producing lung SCC harboring an EGFR S768I mutation. The present findings suggest that the inflammatory and immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment associated with G-CSF and IL-6 production may contribute to resistance against both immune checkpoint inhibitors and EGFR-TKIs, even when targetable mutations are present. CONCLUSION: Although driver mutations are rare in G-CSF-producing lung carcinoma, their presence may not guarantee a good response to targeted therapies. This case underscores the need for careful treatment selection and highlights the importance of further research into the mechanisms of treatment resistance in this intractable phenotype.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: The tumor microenvironment contributes to acquired resistance against osimertinib in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), yet the key cell subpopulations and the underlying metabolic mechanisms remain incompletely elucidated. METHODS: The Scissor algorithm was applied to integrate bulk osimertinib-resistance transcriptomic profiles with single-cell RNA-seq data to pinpoint cell subpopulations functionally associated with the osimertinib resistant phenotype. AddModuleScore was applied to calculate scores for cholesterol metabolism-related modules. Gene-set enrichment analysis was carried out to uncover pathway alterations in osimertinib resistance-related macrophages. Cross-validation was performed in an independent dataset comparing treatment-naive and EGFR-tyrosine kinase inhibitors (EGFR-TKIs)-treated progressive-disease lesions. EGFR-mutant lung adenocarcinoma cells were treated with corresponding conditioned medium combined with osimertinib, followed by a panel of cell function assays, including cell proliferation, colony formation, and apoptosis. The gain- and loss- of function studies of APOE were conducted in THP-1 derived macrophages. RESULTS: Osimertinib-resistant associated Scissor+ cells were mainly enriched within macrophages, which exhibited prominent APOE-dependent cholesterol metabolic reprogramming. APOE was markedly up-regulated in Scissor+ macrophages and macrophages from EGFR-TKI-treated progressive-disease lesions. Macrophage-derived APOE shapes extracellular cholesterol availability in the microenvironment, which may promote intracellular free-cholesterol accumulation in tumor cells and counteract osimertinib-triggered apoptosis. CONCLUSION: APOE-dependent cholesterol metabolic reprogramming in macrophages is associated with osimertinib resistance in NSCLC and may contribute to therapeutic failure. Our results identify APOE as a hypothesis-generating candidate molecule that merits further pre-clinical investigation.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide. Health administrative data (HAD) are increasingly used to identify COPD cases at the population level, yet the diagnostic accuracy of such algorithms remains uncertain. OBJECTIVE: To systematically evaluate the diagnostic performance of validated algorithms using routinely collected HAD to identify prevalent COPD in adult populations, compared with clinical reference standards. METHODS: We conducted a systematic review registered in PROSPERO (CRD42023492921) and reported according to PRISMA-DTA guidelines. PubMed and Embase were searched for studies that validated HAD-based case-detection algorithms for COPD against a clinical or spirometric reference standard, reporting at least one accuracy metric. Data extraction and risk-of-bias assessment followed a tailored QUADAS-2 approach. RESULTS: Twenty-six studies (56,925 reported participants) met the inclusion criteria and contributed 70 algorithm validations. Most were conducted in high-income countries, particularly Canada and Europe, and primarily targeted general or elderly populations. Twenty-one studies (81%) were assigned to the COPD-only group and five (19%) to the group with asthma-inclusive respiratory codes. Among the estimates selected for presentation from nine studies, sensitivity ranged from 38.1% to 85.0% and specificity from 78.4% to 100.0%. Positive predictive values (PPV synthesis, n=12 studies) ranged from 21.7% to 92.0%. High methodological heterogeneity and frequent use of enriched populations limited comparability. Risk of bias was high in the patient-selection and flow-and-timing domains (both 53.8%), mainly due to partial verification and non-representative cohorts. CONCLUSION: Only a minority of available COPD algorithms have undergone robust clinical validation, and their diagnostic performance varies widely across settings. Most studies emphasise specificity over sensitivity. Integrating administrative and clinical electronic data may improve future case-finding accuracy and generalizability for population surveillance.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Pleuroparenchymal fibroelastosis (PPFE) can be idiopathic (iPPFE) or secondary. Although lung transplantation has been established for advanced PPFE, the clinical characteristics and transplantation outcomes of secondary PPFE remain poorly defined. In this study, we evaluated the parameters of secondary PPFE and iPPFE. METHODS: We retrospectively evaluated patients with PPFE who underwent lung transplantation at our institution. The clinical characteristics, transplant outcomes, and longitudinal changes in body mass index (BMI), percent predicted forced vital capacity (%FVC), and the anteroposterior-to-transverse diameter (APDT/TDT) ratio, an indicator of flat chest, were analyzed using linear mixed-effects models. RESULTS: Forty-one patients were included (26 with iPPFE and 15 with secondary PPFE). The underlying cause of secondary PPFE included post-hematopoietic stem cell transplantation in eight patients (53.3%). At baseline, the %FVC (p = 0.017) and APDT/TDT (p = 0.018) were significantly lower in the secondary PPFE group, whereas the BMI did not differ significantly between groups (p = 0.239). Improvements in %FVC tended to be smaller in secondary PPFE at 1 year (estimate: -9.61; p = 0.070) and 2 years (estimate: -10.37; p = 0.067) after transplantation. Longitudinal analysis demonstrated a significant increase in APDT/TDT over time in both groups, whereas the BMI remained stable with no significant group-time interaction. The 5-year overall survival rates were 71.3% and 71.1% in the iPPFE and secondary PPFE groups, respectively, with no significant differences in overall survival (p = 0.624). The 5-year chronic lung allograft dysfunction (CLAD)-free survival rates were 63.7% and 53.9%, respectively, with no significant intergroup difference (p = 0.487). In a Cox proportional hazards model, the hazard ratio for overall survival in the secondary PPFE group compared with the iPPFE group was 1.40 (95% CI, 0.36-5.41; p = 0.625), and for CLAD-free survival was 1.53 (95% CI, 0.46-5.06; p = 0.490). CONCLUSION: Despite severe preoperative restrictive dysfunction and thoracic deformity, patients with secondary PPFE demonstrated post-transplant functional recovery and long-term transplantation outcomes that did not differ significantly from those with iPPFE, although this comparison was limited by the small number of patients with secondary PPFE and should be interpreted with caution.

papers.abstract_en: Polydatin, a natural compound with recognized cardiovascular benefits, has shown preliminary protective effects against pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH), though its underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to investigate its preventive potential and mechanisms as a complementary therapeutic candidate in a monocrotaline (MCT)-induced rat model of PAH. A rat PAH model was established using MCT. Polydatin was administered to evaluate its effects. Right ventricular structure and function were assessed by echocardiography and gross heart specimen analysis. Right ventricular hypertrophy and pulmonary vascular remodeling were assessed by histology and immunohistochemistry. Expression levels of α-SMA, PCNA, and ET-1 were measured. RNA sequencing was performed on lung tissues to identify differentially expressed genes (DEGs). Key targets and pathways were further validated using qPCR and Western blot in both rat lung tissues and primary smooth muscle cells. STEAP4 function was confirmed by siRNA knockdown in primary arterial smooth muscle cells. Polydatin treatment significantly ameliorated PAH, improving right ventricular structure and function, reducing right ventricular hypertrophy (ANP/BNP), and inhibiting pulmonary vascular remodeling (α-SMA, PCNA, and perivascular collagen deposition). RNA sequencing identified DEGs modulated by polydatin, enriched in processes related to cell proliferation and differentiation. STEAP4 was identified as a key target reversed by polydatin at both mRNA and protein levels. Further validation confirmed that polydatin inhibits the activation of the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway and suppresses cell proliferation. siRNA-mediated knockdown of STEAP4 reduced PI3K/AKT phosphorylation and inhibited ASMC proliferation, demonstrating that STEAP4 mediates the anti-proliferative effect of polydatin. Polydatin alleviates MCT-induced PAH and associated vascular remodeling primarily by downregulating STEAP4 and inhibiting the PI3K/AKT pathway. This highlights polydatin's potential as a preventive candidate for PAH.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Diffuse pulmonary ossification (DPO) is a rare interstitial lung disease characterized by ectopic bone formation within the lung parenchyma. Due to its nonspecific clinical and radiological features, DPO is frequently misdiagnosed as pulmonary tuberculosis or other chronic pulmonary infections, particularly in tuberculosis-endemic regions. CASE PRESENTATION: We report a 34-year-old man presenting with intermittent hemoptysis for six months. Chest computed tomography revealed multiple punctate, nodular, and linear high-density lesions with partial calcification, predominantly in the lower lobes and subpleural regions of both lungs. The patient had been repeatedly misdiagnosed with pulmonary tuberculosis at several institutions, despite negative microbiological and bronchoscopic evaluations. Bone scintigraphy demonstrated scattered abnormal pulmonary uptake with mildly increased bone metabolism. Whole-exome sequencing identified a mutation in the MUC5B gene, while no mutation in SLC34A2 was detected. Video-assisted thoracoscopic lung biopsy revealed scattered mature bone and bone marrow tissue within the lung parenchyma, confirming the diagnosis of diffuse pulmonary ossification. After exclusion of secondary causes, idiopathic DPO was diagnosed. No specific treatment was administered, and the patient remained clinically stable during follow-up. CONCLUSIONS: This case highlights that DPO should be considered in patients with diffuse pulmonary calcifications and negative microbiological evidence of infection, particularly in tuberculosis-endemic settings. Bone scintigraphy and surgical lung biopsy may provide important diagnostic value. Notably, the identification of a MUC5B variant suggests a potential link between DPO and fibrotic lung disease, warranting further investigation.

papers.abstract_en: Although exosomes and macrophages have been studied in lung diseases, an integrated framework linking exosomal cargo, macrophage heterogeneity, disease stage, and translational barriers is still lacking. Pulmonary diseases cause substantial morbidity and mortality, and the pulmonary immune microenvironment is shaped by complex cell-cell communication. Lung macrophages are key innate immune cells that display a spectrum of activation states, including M1-like, M2-like, and intermediate phenotypes. This review provides an integrated framework linking exosomal cargo, lung macrophage heterogeneity, signaling crosstalk, disease stage, and translational barriers. We summarize exosome biogenesis and lung macrophage ontogeny, focusing on how exosomes regulate macrophage polarization through NF-κB, PI3K/AKT, JAK/STAT, and ERK pathways and their crosstalk. We then discuss context-dependent effects in lung injury, COPD, asthma, pulmonary fibrosis, and lung cancer. We also review exosome engineering strategies for targeted macrophage modulation. Despite advances, clinical translation is limited by large-scale purification, targeted delivery, safety, and standardized quality control. We conclude that exosome-mediated macrophage regulation is context-dependent and promising, but translation requires MISEV-compliant exosome terminology, rigorous evidence grading, scalable manufacturing, and safe targeted delivery.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) and arterial hypertension frequently coexist and are linked by recurrent nocturnal cardiovascular stress. Intermittent hypoxemia, arousals and intrathoracic pressure swings promote sympathetic activation, vascular dysfunction and abnormal blood-pressure (BP) regulation. AREAS COVERED: This narrative review integrates epidemiological, mechanistic and interventional evidence on the OSA-hypertension relationship based on a PubMed search (start until September 2026). Particular emphasis is placed on nocturnal hypertension, non-dipping, masked and resistant hypertension; the roles of intermittent hypoxemia, sympathetic overactivity, baroreflex, and endothelial dysfunction; and treatment effects of continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP), mandibular advancement devices and weight loss. Evidence from CPAP-withdrawal trials and recent meta-analyses is used to identify characteristics associated with a greater BP response to OSA treatment. EXPERT OPINION: The modest average BP reduction with CPAP conceals substantial heterogeneity. Treatment effects are strongest for nocturnal BP and in patients with uncontrolled BP, severe OSA and sufficient nightly treatment exposure. Future cardiovascular OSA management should move beyond the apnea-hypopnea index toward combined characterization of nocturnal physiological stress, clinical OSA phenotype, BP phenotype, and effective treatment exposure.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: HER2 (ERBB2) alterations in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) comprise a molecularly heterogeneous group, including activating mutations, copy-number gain/amplification, and protein overexpression. HER2 mutation and high-level amplification are generally distinct biological events. HER2-directed antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) have transformed treatment, yet questions remain regarding sequencing, coexisting HER2 alterations, and central nervous system (CNS) progression. CASE DESCRIPTION: A never-smoking woman presented in August 2025 with stage IVB (T4N3M1c2, AJCC v9) right upper-lobe lung adenocarcinoma with nodal, brain, renal, bone, adrenal, and abdominal/retroperitoneal metastases (ECOG 1-2). A 919-gene NGS panel identified an ERBB2 exon 20 insertion, p.Y772_A775dup (VAF 58.4%), with low-level ERBB2 copy-number gain (copy number 3.1); TP53 p.I195T and p.R249S were also detected. PD-L1 tumor proportion score (TPS) was 40%. Because of symptomatic, high-volume disease, cycle 1 (August 31, 2025) consisted of pemetrexed plus carboplatin before biomarker results were available; ivonescimab was added in cycle 2 (September 23, 2025). Restaging on October 15, 2025 showed marked multi-compartment progression: the lung target lesion increased from 4.56 cm to 10.05 cm (>120%), with new brain, renal, and adrenal metastases, retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy, a large right pleural effusion, and deterioration to ECOG 3-4, consistent with hyperprogressive disease (HPD), which was temporally associated with immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) exposure-occurring approximately 3 weeks after the first, and only, dose of ivonescimab and without disease acceleration during the preceding chemotherapy-only cycle. Trastuzumab rezetecan was initiated on October 16, 2025 for six cycles. By December 5, 2025, the lung lesion had shrunk to 5.68 cm with reduced pleural effusion and partial intracranial improvement; best overall response was partial response (PR). Restaging on March 1, 2026 demonstrated spatially heterogeneous progression: thoracic disease and pleural effusion remained controlled, whereas renal, adrenal, retroperitoneal nodal, skeletal, and intracranial lesions progressed, with meningeal enhancement suspicious for leptomeningeal metastasis (lumbar puncture declined). No cranial radiotherapy or surgery was ever administered. Progression-free survival (PFS) was approximately 4.5 months and duration of response (DOR) approximately 2.9 months. Zongertinib 120 mg once daily was started on March 2, 2026, but was discontinued after 7 days because of financial constraints, precluding objective response assessment. The patient died on May 15, 2026, with an overall survival (OS) of approximately 9.5 months. CONCLUSION: In this case of metastatic lung adenocarcinoma with a concurrent ERBB2 exon 20 insertion and low-level copy-number gain, urgent biomarker-agnostic chemo-immunotherapy was followed by HPD after a single ivonescimab cycle, whereas molecularly matched trastuzumab rezetecan produced a rapid partial response with systemic and transient intracranial control before spatially heterogeneous progression emerged. Salvage zongertinib was clinically rational but could not be objectively assessed because of limited exposure. This case highlights how biomarker turnaround time, drug accessibility, and compartment-specific resistance shape the real-world management of HER2-driven NSCLC, and emphasizes the diagnosis of HPD and its temporal association with ICI exposure. The case also has implications for patient selection, supporting early molecular characterization and the prioritization of molecularly matched HER2-directed therapy in patients with actionable oncogenic drivers.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb), the causative agent of tuberculosis (TB) is able to survive and replicate within host cells of the myeloid cell lineage, a critical step in the development of active TB, achieved through multiple immune evasion mechanisms. TRPML1 (Mucolipin 1), a non-selective Ca2+ ion channel belonging to the TRP superfamily, is predominantly expressed in innate immune cells and is localized intracellularly along the endosomal-lysosomal continuum. TRPML1-mediated Ca2+ signalling is vital for lysosomal biogenesis and trafficking processes essential for effective immune responses. The mechanisms regulating TRPML1 channel function in myeloid cells during mycobacterial infection remain poorly characterized. METHODS: During in vitro infection, TRPML1 expression was modulated in a time-dependent manner by Mtb and M. bovis BCG in murine macrophages, as well as in human neutrophils (PMNs) and macrophages (MDMs). Using pharmacological modulation of TRPML1 channel activity, we observed alterations in intracellular Ca2+ concentrations following Mtb infection. RESULTS: Here, we describe distinct TRPML1 expression patterns in granulomas from TB patients who had completed treatment for active TB, suggesting a potential role for TRPML1 in pathogenesis. We further demonstrate that Mtb infection is associated with altered TRPML1 expression and intracellular Ca2+ homeostasis, accompanied by changes in ROS production, necrotic cell death and enhanced mycobacterial survival within host cells. Treatment of PMN-MDM cocultures with a TRPML1 antagonist, but not an agonist, was associated with increased reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels and necrotic cell death. DISCUSSION: Here, we show that Mtb-mediated disruption of TRPML1 function is associated with altered intracellular Ca2+ homeostasis and may contribute to impaired phagosome maturation, a process previously linked to TRPML1-dependent endolysosomal function, thereby potentially favoring mycobacterial survival within host cells. These findings suggest that Mtb-induced alterations in TRPML1 associated cellular Ca²⁺ homeostasis may impair Ca²⁺-dependent ROS production and cell death, potentially affecting intracellular Mtb survival. Our findings support a role for TRPML1 in maintaining myeloid cell Ca²⁺ homeostasis and suggest that TRPML1 may contribute to the innate immune response to Mtb infection.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: The impacts of the ambient environment on asthma have been a topic of extensive research. However, most of this work has explored associations among individuals with asthma on outcomes such as symptoms, hospitalizations and asthma control. This review will focus on the state of the evidence on asthma onset and the ambient environment, highlighting the gaps in the field. AREAS COVERED: This review of articles in English in PubMed published before 10/31/2026 will cover the state of the evidence on impacts of several groups of ambient environmental exposures (air pollution and traffic exposures, climate related factors, ultraviolet radiation, and greenness) on onset of asthma in children and adults. EXPERT OPINION: Compared to the vast literature on the impacts of the ambient environment on individuals, especially children, with asthma, there is far less evidence on the role of the ambient environment as a primary risk factor. Additionally, the literature is dominated by single-exposure studies. Given more recent emphasis in the field on the exposome, or all exposures experienced across the lifecourse, we are likely at a key turning point in the field where the evidence base could and should be built quickly to fill these gaps.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: This study characterized the anatomical features of systemic collateral supply in patients with tuberculosis-related hemoptysis after thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR). It analyzed the technical challenges and strategies of bronchial artery embolization (BAE). The safety and efficacy of adapted embolization strategies were further evaluated. The proposed 3-zone classification for access selection was presented as a hypothesis-generating framework. The findings will inform future management of this complex clinical condition. METHODS: This study analyzed the data of consecutive patients diagnosed with tuberculosis-related hemoptysis after TEVAR who underwent BAE between January 2021 and September 2024. We characterized the anatomical features of systemic collateral supply, applied embolization strategies appropriate to each case. RESULTS: All six patients (mean age 67.3 ± 17.9 years) exhibited systemic collateral supply, with 66.7% (4/6) demonstrating multivessel collateral networks originating from the internal thoracic, esophageal, and inferior phrenic arteries. The transfemoral approach was initially attempted in all cases. It was successful in Cases 1 and 2, but failed in Cases 3-6, requiring conversion to the transradial approach. In the four cases requiring conversion, transfemoral access was attempted for cases 3-6 min before abandonment, whereas subsequent transradial access achieved target selection in 3-15 min. The median dose-area product was 140.85 Gy·cm², in cases with greater anatomical complexity. Longer fluoroscopy times and higher dose-area product (DAP) values were observed. Technical success and immediate hemostasis were achieved in all patients (100%), with no major complications observed in this small case series. CONCLUSION: In this small retrospective case series, systemic collateral supply in tuberculosis-related hemoptysis after TEVAR demonstrates complex anatomical characteristics. BAE was technically feasible for selected patients with tuberculosis-related hemoptysis after TEVAR when guided by CTA-based vascular mapping and individualized access selection. The proposed 3-zone classification offers a potential framework for access planning, though further studies are required to confirm its long-term safety and efficacy.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Pulmonary embolism (PE) is a common respiratory disease that require a thorough etiological workup. However, the pathophysiology of PE in thalassemia patient post-splenectomy can be easily overlooked by pulmonologists. CASE PRESENTATION: A 38-year-old man, who had been diagnosed with α-thalassemia intermedia at 7 months of age, and subsequently underwent splenectomy nine years ago due to severe anemia, developed chest tightness and shortness of breath, and progressed to dyspnea at rest accompanied by dizziness and abdominal pain. Chest and abdomen enhanced CT scan revealed extensive venous thrombosis including pulmonary artery, portal vein, mesenteric vein, hepatic vein and possibly cerebral thrombosis. Cardiac echocardiography demonstrated severe PH (tricuspid-valve regurgitant jet velocity was 4.2 m/s). Investigations including tumor markers, immunological indicators, thrombophilia screen and genetic testing did not elucidate potential provoking factors and pathogeny. Management consisted of curative anticoagulation, antibiotics, diuretics and hyperosmotic dehydration, leading to clinical improvement and subsequent stability on follow-up. CONCLUSION: It is important to recognize PE post splenectomy in patients with thalassemia. It necessitates an integrated, multidisciplinary strategy involving hematology and pulmonology specialists.

papers.abstract_en: Tuberculosis (TB), caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb), remains among the top 10 leading causes of death worldwide, infecting more than 10 million people annually. Upon inhalation into the host lungs, Mtb is internalized by alveolar macrophages, where it deploys complex strategies to evade the host immune response and enhance its intracellular survival. This review synthesizes the current understanding of the major molecular pathways driving Mtb's intracellular persistence, focusing on its ability to disrupt phagolysosomal maturation and autophagic pathways, while also manipulating host apoptotic pathways. Furthermore, we detail how these mechanisms are aided by genetic and epigenetic manipulations within the host macrophages, such as the silencing of antimicrobial peptides, downregulation of transcriptional regulators, and the use of non-coding RNAs. Understanding these host-pathogen interfaces provides targets for the development of host directed therapies (HDTs) which can overcome the survival mechanisms that make Mtb so resilient to classical antibiotics.
